title: Jackson's cruelty, the school band and learning a tune by ear
summary: He recalls Jackson stamping on his feet, the little school band, and the day he heard someone practice a solo and realized he could play tunes by ear.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: Learning your horn: teachers, lessons and fees

blocks.x: So it was strictly one of those schools, you know, a bunch of kids. And they formed a little band, and we did one or two concerts after I'd been with them for a year. So, but I always wanted to play something with a sound. And naturally, just playing trombone parts, they don't sound like nothing. Even the little orchestrations that we would play in this little orchestra set up, there never was any melody, or any tune or anything connected to it. So my mother had been sacrificing and sending me to take these lessons. And after a couple of years, she said, well, when are you going to play a tune? So I tried to instill in her. I said, well, Mama, I'm playing the notes. You see the notes? She said, but it don't sound like nothing. There's no tune anything to it, see. So I would save up my little money and go down the line and heal in and buy orchestrations, which I thought would be the right thing. Well, when I'd get home with them and play the trombone parts, I could play the parts very easily. But there still wasn't any musical sound to it. It was just fill in parts, you know, the type of thing that trombone plays. So it had never once dawned on me that I could maybe just concentrate and play something from hearing it. So one day I happened to be out. I was doing the summer vacation out from school. And I was out looking for a job. I was way over north someplace. I don't have any idea what vicinity. But I went over to ask an ad for a porter and a drugstore. And I'm walking down the streets and I hear somebody playing a solo. The solo was Brunus' solo of Ten Loof Blue. Now I've had the record at home because I used to buy all those records and everything. But that was the first time that the idea dawned on me that anybody else could play that same thing other than the man that played it on the record. So I had this fellow, whoever it was, was just in the house and he was practicing this solo. I said, well if he can do it, I can go on home and do it. So consequently when I did get home that afternoon I picked out my own and found out I could play it just from here. Like that, you know. So from then on I could keep them happy around the house. I mean I could play some form of a melody or something, you know.
